questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving types — number isnan.

options.misconception: Assuming dividing a number by text yields a number
Confusing the test with the value tested

questions.explanation: Dividing 394 by a non-numeric string produces NaN, and Number.isNaN returns true for that value. The global isNaN would first coerce, which differs from the strict method. The printed value is true, while the alternatives come from assuming dividing a number by text yields a number, confusing the test with the value tested and thinking the conversion throws.
questions.hint: Number.isNaN does not coerce its argument.

questions.explanation: for...of iterates the element values, adding 396, 2 and 3 to reach 401. Unlike for...in, it does not visit property keys. Both the direct number 401 and the equivalent sum 200 plus 201 match, whereas 396 and 399 come from counting only the first value and skipping the value two.
questions.hint: for...of yields values, not indexes.

options.misconception: Treating a zero delay as immediate

questions.explanation: setTimeout schedules its callback as a macrotask, so both synchronous logs finish before 399 appears. A delay of zero does not mean run right now. The printed value is 1 3 399, while the alternatives come from treating a zero delay as immediate, reversing the synchronous statements and placing the timer callback first.
questions.hint: Timers run after the current synchronous stack clears.
